claims.claim_text: The indexed Sarah J Sillcocks is confirmed as Sarah (Sally) Sillcocks, who worked in the OSS Art Looting Investigation Unit.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A NARA archival essay explicitly expands Sally Sillcocks to Sarah J. Sillcocks and places her in ALIU; Princeton independently documents the same OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact indexed name, NARA's explicit name expansion and independent institutional OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources document ALIU work from 1944 onward but do not identify her immediate pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The postwar Princeton career is not used as pre-OSS evidence.

claims.claim_text: Vassar College identifies Sarah J. Sillcocks as a member of the class of 1935.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Vassar's institutional exhibition record identifies Sarah J. Sillcocks Graham as class of 1935; NARA and Princeton establish the same woman's OSS identity.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact full name, married-name bridge and independently confirmed Sarah/Sally Sillcocks identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation; not employment and not shown to be immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Vassar is classified as an educational institution for this claim, not an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed French Lieutenant Roger Siffredi probably matches Roger Marc Siffredi, whose two French military-archive finding-aid entries identify wartime resistance-related files.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Both French finding aids identify Roger Marc Siffredi, born 2 January 1915 in Marseille; the OSS index supplies the rare name, lieutenant rank and French note.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable, not confirmed: the rare name and French wartime context align, but no reviewed source supplies Box 710 or a shared protected identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The French registers document wartime file contexts but do not identify a pre-OSS employer, unit or sequence into OSS.
claims.match_notes: The two archival files should be reviewed before assigning a resistance organization, employer or immediate predecessor.

claims.claim_text: The index prints Signal in the surname column and Section in the given-name column, producing a non-person-form entry that remains unresolved.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rendered table shows Signal / Section as a separate Box 710 row between Morris A Sigh and Domenico G Signore.
claims.identity_match_assessment: No person is asserted; the row is preserved as an explicit unresolved entity pending examination of Box 710.
claims.temporal_assessment: No chronology or employer can be assigned to an organizational-looking index entry.
claims.match_notes: Do not silently delete the row or fabricate a personal biography. Signal Section is retained as a search variant.
